# Main Street competitive mode: AI opponent on the shared street

## Problem Statement

Main Street is single-player only; the `MainStreetState`, `MainStreetEngine`, and PRD M3 were never designed for an opponent. Players asked for competitive play — racing an AI on the shared street grid — but the engine assumes single ownership of coins, hand, actions, street slots, and score. Adding competitive mode requires splitting those concerns while preserving single-player behaviour and the existing AI/hint/Monte Carlo stack.

## Users & User Stories

- **Player (competitive mode):** As a Main Street player, I want to play against an AI opponent on the same shared street so each turn I have a rival to race and react to.
- **Developer / QA:** As a developer, I want a head-to-head Monte Carlo harness for competitive mode so balance between player and AI can be measured across seeded runs.
- **Future AI iteration:** As an AI developer, I want the AI decision layer ownership-aware and staff-free so competitive strategy is coherent without rewriting the hint/balance harness.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1 — Per-player state & ownership:** A competitive state model exists with per-player coins/reputation, hand, staff, action budget, and score, plus owner-tagged street slots; deterministic and replayable via seeded RNG. Single-player behaviour is unchanged.
- [ ] **AC2 — AI plays a legal competitive turn:** The AI generates legal actions through `enumerateLegalActions` (competitive mode) with staff actions excluded, scored by an ownership-aware `scoreAction`/helpers, and executed via `executeAction`. Verified with legality and determinism tests.
- [ ] **AC3 — Per-owner income; shared events:** Income accrues only to the owning player of each placed business; street-wide investment events and incidents retain their existing resolution semantics, routed per-owner as specified. Validated by income/event unit tests.
- [ ] **AC4 — Competitive Monte Carlo harness:** A head-to-head harness (extending `MainStreetMonteCarlo`) runs >=200 seeds and produces win/score distributions plus per-player metrics; single-player AI tests still pass.
- [ ] **AC5 — Engine-only scope confirmed:** PRD M3 is updated to note this deliberate scope extension; competitive mode has no game-selector entry or scene yet — rendering (owner-coloured street, shared-market phase alternation with SFX/animations per AGENTS.md 8) is deferred to a planning-created child.
- [ ] **AC6 — Tests & docs:** Relevant unit tests and new tests cover AC1–AC4; build succeeds; affected docs/comments are updated.
- [ ] **AC7 — Full test suite passes** with the new changes (release gate; not a per-push requirement beyond `npm run build` + unit tests).

## Constraints

- Competitive mode scope is **state + engine + AI + Monte Carlo only** — no game selector entry, no competitive scene, no competitive UI chrome yet (AC5 deferred to a planning child).
- Turn alternation: **alternate MarketPhases within a shared day** (confirmed producer decision). Income/Incident/EndCheck phases are shared once both players have acted. Implementation design stays within planning.
- Win condition: **first player to reach the win threshold wins**; the game offers an endless continuation option beyond threshold (confirmed producer decision). Endless mode wiring is within the parent unless planning creates a dedicated child.
- `MainStreetAiPlayer` / `MainStreetAiStrategy` / `GreedyStrategy` / `scoreAction` / `enumerateLegalActions` are unchanged for single-player consumers.
- Determinism via seeded RNG is preserved; replays remain reproducible.

## Existing State

- Single-player-only state (`MainStreetState` resourceBank/hand/staffCards/actionsRemaining), engine (`applyIncome`, `resolveEvent`, `resolveIncident`, `computeScore`, `checkEndConditions`), PRD M3, and AI layers (`MainStreetAiStrategy`, `GreedyStrategy`, `scoreAction`, `MainStreetAiPlayer`, `MainStreetMonteCarlo`) built for one owner. Reusability findings documented in the original description.
- One child item already exists: **CG-0MT5X3N79002S038 — Competitive AI strategy (ownership-aware, staff-free)**.

## Desired Change

Ship an **engine-level competitive mode**: per-player state + owner-tagged grid, per-owner income routing, shared event semantics, ownership-aware and staff-free AI scoring, and a competitive Monte Carlo harness — without changing single-player behaviour or adding competitive rendering. Record the scope extension in PRD M3 and plan the rendering/scene child for the next milestone.

## Decisions Since Original Item

- **Turn structure:** Option A (alternate MarketPhases within a shared day) confirmed by producer.
- **AC5:** Deferred to planning — will become a child for rendering/selector/scene work.
- **Denial reasoning:** Opponent-aware denial (blocking best slot, buying to deny) intentionally deferred to a follow-up child.
- **Win condition:** First to threshold wins, with an endless continuation option beyond threshold.
- **Owner-coloured street (AC5):** Means tinting each placed business's street slot by owner (e.g., player = blue, AI = red) so the shared grid's ownership is visually unambiguous.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — Split to per-player resources/hand/staff/actions/score; owner-tagged `StreetGrid` slots.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — Per-owner income, shared event/incident routing, shared-day phase handling, competitive helpers.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — Ownership-aware `scoreAction`/per-type helpers + competitive `enumerateLegalActions` variant (staff excluded); single-player paths unchanged.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — Competitive head-to-head harness (extension).
- `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-3.md` — Note competitive mode as deliberate scope extension beyond M3.
- `tests/main-street/*.test.ts` (+ new competitive tests) — Unit + deterministic replay coverage for AC1–AC4; existing guardrails still passing.

## Related Work

- Related work items (from `find_related`): CG-0MM5ZGB8U02S0BFO — Main Street Scenario & Tutorial (completed) · CG-0MOXGGZXJ002X6H3 — [test-failure] MainStreetScene animation scheduling (completed) · CG-0MS9NXIEX00880UV — [test-failure] hud-layer-contract (completed)
- Related docs (from repo scan): `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-3.md` · `docs/DEVELOPER.md` · `AGENTS.md`
- Child: CG-0MT5X3N79002S038 — Competitive AI strategy (existing; align description with this parent's clarified ACs).
- Existing state/engine/AI/monte-carlo layers are the implementation basis (see Existing State above).

## Risks & Assumptions

- **State split regressions in single player:** score/income/event paths silently ignore per-player split. Mitigation: keep single-player API shim and run full single-player regression suite.
- **Income/event routing divergence:** per-owner bugs hard to diagnose. Mitigation: explicit per-owner unit fixtures + deterministic replay across seeds.
- **AI ownership semantics under-tested:** greedy heuristics mis-score denial/synergy when ownership added. Mitigation: head-to-head harness + baseline comparisons (AC4).
- **Phase alternation complexity:** alternating MarketPhases within one day adds state machine edge cases. Mitigation: diagram shared-day phases in planning and cover transitions with unit tests.
- **Scope creep toward rendering:** temptation to start the selector/scene early. Mitigation: AC5 is explicitly deferred; new rendering asks become planning-linked children.

## Open Questions

None — all open intake questions have been answered by the producer (see Comments). Remaining design detail (per-player state shape, phase machine, Monte Carlo metrics schema, endless-mode trigger) is within planning.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q1 (Map, via `wl comment add CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30`): "Alternating turn structure — Option A (alternate MarketPhases within a shared day) vs Option B (alternate full days)?" — Answer (producer, 2026-09-01): "a" → resolved as **Option A** (alternate MarketPhases within a shared day). Recorded in `wl comment` (producer decisions comment).
- Q2 (Map, via `wl comment add CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30`): "Child item coverage for AC5 — create competitive-scene child now or defer to planning?" — Answer (producer): "planning. for now what do you mean by 'owner colored streets'" → resolved as **deferred to planning**; follow-up clarification Q5 added. Recorded in `wl comment`.
- Q3 (Map, via `wl comment add CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30`): "Denial reasoning scope — deferred or minimum viable?" — Answer (producer): "deferred" → denial is **out of scope** for this epic, may become a follow-up child.
- Q4 (Map, via `wl comment add CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30`): "Win condition — first to threshold, fixed days, or simultaneous?" — Answer (producer): "when one player rea hes a win conditiion with option to carry on in endless mode" → **first to threshold wins, with endless continuation option**.
- Q5 (Map, implicit follow-up): "What does 'owner coloured streets' mean?" — Answer purpose: rendering the shared street grid where each placed business slot is visually tinted by owner (e.g., player blue, AI red) so ownership is immediately readable. Scene concern deferred to planning child.

## Goal (user story)

As a developer of the competitive mode, I want the balancing AI's decision layer (`MainStreetAiStrategy` / `GreedyStrategy` / `scoreAction` / `MainStreetAiPlayer`) adapted to shared-street competitive semantics, so the opponent plays competently on a street it does not fully own.

## Context

The existing heuristics assume the AI owns the whole street:
- `scoreBusinessAction` / `scorePlayBusinessFromHandAction` value `(income + synergy) * horizon - cost` with no ownership concept.
- `aiPlanningHorizon` measures distance to the win threshold via `computeScore`, which sums a single player's coins + reputation.
- `enumerateLegalActions` includes staff actions (`hire-staff`, `peek-incident-deck`) — competitive mode makes staff player-only.

Parent: Main Street competitive mode epic (CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30). Depends on per-owner income routing (sibling) so scoring can evaluate against the acting player's own resources.

## Scope

- Ownership-aware scoring: evaluate income, synergy, and horizon against the **AI's own** resources/businesses and its own win threshold (using the per-player state model from the competitive state sibling).
- Staff exclusion: competitive-mode action enumeration drops staff actions from the AI's option space.
- Determinism via seeded RNG is preserved.

## Out of scope

- Opponent-aware *denial* reasoning (blocking the opponent's best slot, buying to deny) — intentionally deferred to a follow-up child.
- Endless continuation — deferred to a separate top-level issue.
- N-player Monte Carlo — covered by the Monte Carlo harness sibling; architecture is N-player-ready (PlayerRecord[] indexed by owner) but the initial harness validates head-to-head (1 human vs 1 AI).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** `scoreAction` and the per-type scoring helpers evaluate placement/upgrade/event value using only the acting player's resources and owned businesses, with the planning horizon computed from the acting player's own score vs. their win threshold.
- [ ] **AC2:** Competitive-mode legal-action enumeration excludes `hire-staff` and staff-skill actions (peek), while the single-player enumeration is unchanged.
- [ ] **AC3:** Deterministic: same seed + same strategy produces identical action sequences; verified by a dedicated deterministic replay test.
- [ ] **AC4:** All existing single-player AI tests (`ai-strategy.test.ts`, hint consistency, balance guardrails) still pass unchanged.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — Ownership-aware `scoreAction`/per-type helpers + competitive `enumerateLegalActions` variant (staff excluded); single-player paths unchanged.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-ai-strategy.test.ts` — Dedicated competitive AI tests (ownership-aware scoring, staff exclusion, determinism).

## Related Work

- Parent: CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30 — Main Street competitive mode: AI opponent on the shared street
- Depends on: competitive state model + income/event routing siblings (per-player resources/score needed for ownership-aware horizon)

## Goal (user story)

As a developer, I want income to accrue only to the owning player of each placed business and shared events/incidents to retain their existing semantics routed per-owner, so the competitive economy is legible and testable.

## Context

`applyIncome` / adjacency income and `resolveEvent`/`resolveIncident` are single-player (one resourceBank/finalScore). Once street slots are owner-tagged (state-model sibling) and the phase machine delegates Income/Incident to per-owner handlers, the routing must be precise. Incident/Investment event regression risk: silent divergence where the wrong owner is credited or both are affected.

## Scope

- Per-owner income: each placed business's income (base + adjacency + upgrades + salary/ongoing) accrues only to its slot owner.
- Shared events/incidents: street-wide Investment events and incidents retain existing resolution semantics, routed per-owner as specified (design within planning: per-owner effects vs. shared board effects).
- Single-player (N=1) income path unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Phase machine / win condition (sibling).
- AI strategy / Monte Carlo.
- Endless continuation (deferred).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** Income for each placed business accrues only to the owning player (verified by per-owner fixtures covering base + synergy + upgrade + salary/ongoing).
- [ ] **AC2:** Shared Investment events and incidents retain existing resolution semantics and are routed per-owner as specified (design within planning); verified by per-owner event unit tests.
- [ ] **AC3:** Deterministic replay: same seed → identical per-owner income/event sequences.
- [ ] **AC4:** N=1 regression: income/event behaviour matches the pre-competitive single-player baseline.

## Goal (user story)

As a player, I want the competitive game to offer an endless continuation option beyond the win threshold (producer Q4: “option to carry on in endless mode”), so we can keep building after someone wins.

## Context

Competitive mode's win condition is first-to-threshold (parent CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30, phase-machine sibling). The producer explicitly asked for an endless continuation beyond threshold. Planning deferred this to a separate top-level issue (not a child of the competitive epic) so the competitive epic stays engine-focused and endless mode can land independently. N-player-ready design (PlayerRecord[]) is already in scope for the competitive architecture.

## Scope

- Endless-mode trigger and state handling after the win threshold is first reached (continue playing beyond threshold; scoring/phase semantics while beyond threshold).
- How the UI/scene signals “winner declared but still playing” (if any UI is needed here; full competitive rendering is the separate CG-0MTIILOLR002ZU9K child).
- Whether endless mode needs its own Monte Carlo treatment or is validated by manual play.

## Out of scope

- Competitive state model / phase machine / income routing / AI / harness / rendering — those are CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30 and its children.
- Denial reasoning (separate follow-up).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** Endless mode wiring is defined via an explicit opt-in flag/config: what triggers continuation, what happens to win detection/score/endReason/gameResult when play continues beyond threshold.
- [ ] **AC2:** Deterministic behaviour — same seed + same actions produce the same endless-mode outcome.
- [ ] **AC3:** Competitive mode remains playable without engaging endless mode (players can stop at the threshold win; default behaviour unchanged).

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetState.ts` — Endless-mode flag/state.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngine.ts` — Win detection vs. continue-beyond-threshold semantics.
- `tests/main-street/competitive-endless.test.ts` — Dedicated endless-mode tests (threshold win vs. continuation).

# Intake Brief — Change the name of the Physiotherapy business card to Physiotherapist

**Work item:** CG-0MTRRYOT6001167R
**Issue type:** task · **Priority:** low
**Headline:** The Main Street business card `biz-physio` is displayed as "Physiotherapy" (the treatment) instead of "Physiotherapist" (the practitioner); correct the display name everywhere and drop the now-redundant art alias.

## Problem statement

The Main Street business card with `id=biz-physio` is named **"Physiotherapy"**, which is the treatment rather than the profession/practitioner. Every other business card is named for the business or practitioner, and the card's already-committed art sprite is `Physiotherapist_1024_x_1024.png`. The mismatch is papered over by a spelling alias (`Physiotherapy` → `Physiotherapist`) in the card-art pipeline. The card's display name should be corrected to **"Physiotherapist"** across data, generated assets, tests, and documentation, and the redundant alias removed.

## Users

- **Main Street players** — see the card name on the card face, in the market, in hand, and in tooltips; expect it to read as a business/profession.
- **Developers / content authors** — expect the CSV `name` field to match the committed sprite base name so no alias is required.

### User stories

- As a Main Street player, I see the business card named **"Physiotherapist"** on the card face so the card reads as a profession, consistent with the rest of the business deck.
- As a developer, I can rely on `card-data.csv` `name` matching the sprite base name `Physiotherapist`, so the `Physiotherapy → Physiotherapist` alias is no longer needed.
- As a maintainer, I can regenerate the SVG card faces and the art map from the CSV with no manual name fix-ups.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **CSV data** — The `id=biz-physio` row in `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` has `name=Physiotherapist`; the display string `Physiotherapy` no longer appears in `card-data.csv`.
2. **Generated card face** — `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/biz-physio.svg` regenerated from the CSV contains `aria-label="Physiotherapist"` and card-title text `Physiotherapist`; `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/csv-checksum.json` matches the new CSV checksum.
3. **Art resolution** — `CARD_ART_ALIASES` in `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` no longer contains a `Physiotherapy` entry, `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` is regenerated accordingly, and `resolveCardArtName('Physiotherapist')` / `hasDedicatedCardArt('Physiotherapist')` still resolve to dedicated (non-`Fallback`) art.
4. **References updated** — All display-name references in tests and docs are updated (`tests/main-street/group-a-business-expansion.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts`, `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md`, `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md`); no `Physiotherapy` remains in source, tests, docs, or generated assets.
5. **Validation** — Unit tests for Main Street pass (`npx vitest run --project unit tests/main-street/`) and the production build succeeds (`npm run build`); the full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
6. **Documentation** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the change, including code comments, `README`, and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries (the card catalog and content-design docs above are the primary sites).

## Constraints

- **Do NOT change the card `id`** (`biz-physio`). It is a stable identifier used by saves, tier maps, manifests, and tests; renaming it would break persistence and is out of scope.
- **Do NOT rename sprite files.** `sprites/Physiotherapist_1024_x_1024.png` already uses the target name.
- **Regenerate, do not hand-edit generated artefacts**: `node scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` (card SVGs + `csv-checksum.json`) and `node scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` (`card-art-map.json`, after removing the alias from the script).
- Art must remain resolvable — no regression to the generic `Fallback` sprite.
- Follow the repo doc-update policy for any workflow/tooling implications.

## Existing state

- Committed sprite: `example-games/main-street/sprites/Physiotherapist_1024_x_1024.png` (already target-named).
- Alias introduced by CG-0MTORJ5FS006B0UN: `'Physiotherapy': 'Physiotherapist'` in `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` (`CARD_ART_ALIASES`), mirrored in generated `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` (`aliases`).
- Display-name occurrence sites today:
  - `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` (1 row, `name` field).
  - `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/biz-physio.svg` (aria-label + title text — generated).
  - `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` (alias — generated).
  - `tests/main-street/group-a-business-expansion.test.ts` (expected `name`).
  - `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` (alias-resolution assertion).
  - `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` (4 references).
  - `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` (1 reference).
- `docs/main-street/expanded-card-manifest.json` and `card-catalog-baseline.json` reference only the `id`/counts — no change expected.

## Desired change

Rename the `biz-physio` card's display name to **"Physiotherapist"** in the CSV, regenerate the committed SVG card face and `csv-checksum.json`, remove the redundant `Physiotherapy` alias from the art-map generator and regenerate `card-art-map.json`, update the affected tests and docs, and keep card art resolution intact.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — change the `name` field for `biz-physio` to `Physiotherapist`.
- `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` — remove the `'Physiotherapy': 'Physiotherapist'` alias entry.
- `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` — regenerate (alias removed; `Physiotherapist` art key already present).
- `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/biz-physio.svg` — regenerate (title/aria-label).
- `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/csv-checksum.json` — regenerate checksum.
- `tests/main-street/group-a-business-expansion.test.ts` — update expected card `name`.
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` — update the alias-resolution assertion (assert exact-match resolution for `Physiotherapist`).
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — update 4 references.
- `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` — update 1 reference.

## Related work

- **CG-0MTORJ5FS006B0UN** (completed) — Main Street card-art redesign; introduced `CARD_ART_ALIASES` including `Physiotherapy → Physiotherapist`. This item removes that alias by aligning the CSV name.
- **CG-0MUBVL4H80061B1E** (open) — Assign a dedicated sprite to every Main Street card; this rename keeps `biz-physio` on its dedicated sprite.
- **CG-0MTRRYOT6001167R** — this item.

### Related work (automated `find-related` report)

Keyword scan (`business`, `card`, `change`, `name`, `physiotherapist`, `physiotherapy`) returned the following, none of which are direct dependencies of this rename:

- **CG-0MSKU0BE5003I2ZD** (completed) — Main Street combined business/held-event hand; touches business-card UI but not naming.
- **CG-0MQRXN2CT0076OW7** (completed) — Multi-Use Card Economy; touches card economics, not naming.
- **CG-0MQK73QQP005O4OQ** (completed) — Lighting spike; unrelated (keyword noise).
- Repository file matches (`AGENTS.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `README.md`) are generic keyword hits and require no change.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** Changing `card-data.csv` changes `CSV_CHECKSUM`, which flags existing saves as stale. **Mitigation:** regeneration updates `csv-checksum.json`; the existing save-mismatch handling in `MainStreetLifecycleManagerCampaign` already covers this, and card data changes routinely trigger the same path.
- **Risk:** Forgetting to regenerate the committed SVG leaves a stale "Physiotherapy" title on the card face. **Mitigation:** AC2 explicitly checks the generated SVG.
- **Risk:** Removing the alias while the CSV rename is incomplete would drop `biz-physio` to `Fallback` art. **Mitigation:** do the CSV rename and regeneration together; AC3 guards art resolution.
- **Assumption:** Only the display `name` changes — the `id` (`biz-physio`) and sprite filenames stay unchanged.
- **Assumption:** The redundant alias is removed rather than retained (keeping it would leave dead mapping and a stale test).
- **Scope-creep:** Other spelling aliases (`Community Renovation`, `Labor Shortage`, `Neighborhood Watch`, `Graffiti`) are out of scope; record separately if desired.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required — the seed intent ("Change the name of the Physiotherapy business card to Physiotherapist") is unambiguous. The assumptions above (id unchanged, sprite unchanged, alias removed, generated artefacts regenerated) were derived from repository inspection rather than producer input.

- Q: "Should the internal card id `biz-physio` also change?" — Answer (agent, from repo inspection): No. The id is referenced by saves, `CARD_TIER_MAP`, `expanded-card-manifest.json`, `design-12-tiers.py`, and tests; it is a stable identifier. Source: `rg -n "biz-physio"`.
- Q: "Do the sprites need renaming?" — Answer (agent, from repo inspection): No. `sprites/Physiotherapist_1024_x_1024.png` already uses the target name. Source: `ls example-games/main-street/sprites/`.
- Q: "Is the `Physiotherapy` art alias still needed after the rename?" — Answer (agent, from repo inspection): No. Once the CSV name is `Physiotherapist`, it matches the sprite base name exactly, so the alias becomes dead. Source: `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs:88`.

# Add a Charity Shop business card (MS-0MUAYBAHW007RMSL) — Intake brief

## Problem statement

Main Street has no charity shop: a low-cost, Culture-synergy business that trades a modest income for a steady reputation trickle. The producer has specified the card's core economy (1.5 income/turn, 0.15 reputation/turn, cost 3 at the pre-scale convention), and this work adds the card to the pool so players gain an early reputation-leaning Culture business at tier 2.

## Users (example user stories)

- **As a player**, I can buy a Charity Shop for 300 coins and place it on the street, where it produces a small income and a steady reputation gain each turn, giving me an early Culture-synergy building with a reputation focus.
- **As a player**, I expect the Charity Shop to participate in Culture adjacency synergy like other Culture businesses (Bookshop, Craft Shop), so I can cluster it with my Culture cards.
- **As a maintainer**, I expect the new card to be a first-class registered template — present in the CSV, the tier/progression system, generated metadata and card art — with all template-count and consistency tests updated rather than special-cased.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Card data.** `src/card-data.csv` contains a new business row with exactly: `family = business`, `id = biz-charity-shop`, `name = Charity Shop`, `cost = 300`, `baseIncome = 150`, `synergyTypes = Culture`, `upgradePath = Charity Shop`, `maxLevel = 1`, `reputationPerTurn = 15`, `ongoingCost = 75`, `tier = 2`, plus a non-empty `description` and `art_notes`.
2. **Registered template.** The card is loaded by `MainStreetCards.ts` as a business template, is available at tier 2 through the tier/`CARD_TIER_MAP` progression, and appears in the business deck built by `createBusinessDeck()`.
3. **Generated metadata and art.** `docs/main-street/expanded-card-manifest.json` lists `biz-charity-shop` under `expandedCardIds.business`, and `node src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` produces `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/biz-charity-shop.svg`; both are committed.
4. **Tests.** Automated tests assert the Charity Shop's `cost`, `baseIncome`, `reputationPerTurn`, `ongoingCost`, `synergyTypes` and `tier`, and every hardcoded count affected by adding one business template is updated:
   - business-template count `30 → 31` in `game-state.test.ts` (`BUSINESS_TEMPLATE_COUNT`), `expanded-card-pool.test.ts`, `group-a-business-expansion.test.ts` (test title/comment too), and the `createBusinessDeck(1).length` assertions in the `group-b`…`group-f` expansion tests;
   - aggregate pool totals in `meta-progression.test.ts`: tier-12 `cumulativeCardIds` `173 → 174` and unique base-id `allBaseIds.size` `165 → 166`;
   - the hardcoded tier-2 synergy snapshot in `tier-synergy-balance.test.ts` becomes `{ Commerce: 2, Service: 1, Culture: 1 }`.
   The full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
5. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` (business table, deck-size/expansion counts, synergy-type coverage) and any relevant README or docs-site entries. **Note:** `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded — managed by the ship skill's release pipeline.

## Constraints

- **×100 integer economy** (CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6): all coin/reputation CSV values are integers at 100× the design scale — `cost 300`, `baseIncome 150`, `reputationPerTurn 15`. No fractional values anywhere in the CSV.
- **Ongoing cost convention** (CG-0MSVYPEZ90085SHE): businesses pay ¼ of purchase price per turn (min 25), so `ongoingCost = 75`; the card is charged this while in hand or on the street.
- **Card text must match data** (`card-text-data-consistency` test): the `description` reputation figure must equal the `reputationPerTurn` value and the synergy sentence must match the Culture synergy.
- **Tier-2 synergy balance** (`tier-synergy-balance.test.ts`, ≤2× ratio): tier 2 becomes Commerce 2 / Service 1 / Culture 1 — ratio 2.0, which passes.
- **Tier family balance** (`tier-family-balance.test.ts`, ≤46% per family): tier 2 business share becomes 4/22 ≈ 18.2% — passes.
- **Producer-specified cost override:** the balance curve (`tier*2 + 2 + baseIncome*4 + …`) would price this card higher than 300; the producer's explicit `cost 3` (300) takes precedence and is recorded as a deliberate manual override, not a curve result.

## Existing state

- There is **no** charity shop / thrift / op-shop card in `card-data.csv` or `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md`; this is a net-new template.
- The pool currently has **30 business templates**; tier 2 contains Hardware Store (Service), Pawn Shop (Commerce) and Boutique (Commerce).
- Business cards are generic CSV-driven templates; `MainStreetCards.ts` parses rows, and per-tier registration is derived from the CSV `tier` column (`CARD_TIER_MAP`) — no bespoke TypeScript class is needed.
- Tests hardcode both the business-template count (`30`) **and aggregate pool totals** (tier-12 cumulative `173`, unique base-id set `165`), and `docs/main-street/expanded-card-manifest.json` enumerates every non-baseline business id (currently 26 business ids; with the 4 tier-1 baseline business ids the total is 30) — all must be updated. `tier-synergy-balance.test.ts` also hardcodes the per-tier synergy snapshot.
- Business card art resolves through `card-art-map.json` with a generic `Fallback` sprite when a dedicated 1024×1024 sprite is absent.

## Desired change

Add the Charity Shop as a tier-2 Culture business template with the values in AC1, regenerate the derived metadata and SVG card artifacts, update the hardcoded business-count assertions and the catalog documentation, and add/extend tests asserting the new card's economy.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — add the `biz-charity-shop` business row.
- `docs/main-street/expanded-card-manifest.json` — regenerate via `npx vite-node src/scripts/generate-main-street-expanded-card-manifest.ts` (business id list grows 26 → 27).
- `public/assets/games/main-street/svg/cards/biz-charity-shop.svg` — generated by `node src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — add the card to the tier-2 business table; update the two deck-size tables (Business 30 → 31, business cards 90 → 93), the expansion summary (Business 30 → 31, total 157 → 158, net +142 → +143) and the synergy-type coverage table (Culture single 4 → 5; Culture total 10 → 11).
- `tests/main-street/game-state.test.ts` — `BUSINESS_TEMPLATE_COUNT` 30 → 31.
- `tests/main-street/group-a-business-expansion.test.ts` — business template count 30 → 31 (and wording/comment).
- `tests/main-street/expanded-card-pool.test.ts` — business template count 30 → 31 (and test description).
- `tests/main-street/group-b-community-space-expansion.test.ts`, `group-c-investment-events-expansion.test.ts`, `group-d-incident-events-expansion.test.ts`, `group-e-upgrade-cards-expansion.test.ts`, `group-f-staff-abilities-expansion.test.ts` — `createBusinessDeck(1).length` 30 → 31.
- `tests/main-street/meta-progression.test.ts` — tier-12 `cumulativeCardIds` 173 → 174 (test title/comment too) and `allBaseIds.size` 165 → 166.
- `tests/main-street/tier-synergy-balance.test.ts` — extend the hardcoded sparse-tier snapshot for `'tier-2'` with `Culture: 1` (and update the header comment); optionally add a Charity Shop synergy assertion.
- `tests/main-street/card-manifest.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/card-svg-coverage.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/tier-family-balance.test.ts` — driven by the regenerated artifacts/CSV; verify they pass.
- `tests/main-street/card-text-data-consistency.test.ts` — verifies card text matches data; passes once `description`/`art_notes` match the values in AC1.
- `docs/main-street/balancing-methodology.md` — add a Special Cases note for the producer's manual cost override (if the balance doc is maintained against the CSV).

## Related work

> The `CG-` ids below are from the legacy Tableau-Card-Engine (core) worklog; the same content was migrated to this repo under the `MS-` prefix (see the migration comment on this item).

- `CG-0MUAYBA0L000XLK3` — Pawn shop should reduce, not increase reputation (sibling migrated producer note; establishes the ×100 value convention for business cards).
- `CG-0MTIO1M15001E9Y6` — integer economy (coin/rep ×100).
- `CG-0MSVYPEZ90085SHE` — business ongoing cost (¼ purchase price, min 25).
- `CG-0MUIH30NQ0047W1I` — Reconcile event card text to integer data; `CG-0MTW1EN0D003CSA0` — validate all card text.
- `CG-0MT3IPFSF005KEFB` — tier synergy-type balance rule (constrains tier-2 placement).
- `CG-0MT3C744B009DS84` / `CG-0MT2WU0CX005Z143` — 12-tier progression and family rebalance.
- Automated related-work report: `CG-0MSQE2NLX003ADIY` (Main Street: design 50+ new cards), `CG-0MMJTGQFE1RL6VJA` (synergy icons in help panel).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption (producer-confirmed, Q2):** synergy type is **Culture** (a charity shop might thematically read as Commerce; overridden by the producer's answer).
- **Assumption (producer-confirmed, Q3):** **tier 2, standalone** (`maxLevel = 1`, no upgrade chain).
- **Assumption (producer-confirmed, Q1):** 1.5 is **gross** `baseIncome`; the standard 75 ongoing cost applies on top (net 0.75/turn).
- **Assumption (not explicitly confirmed; low risk):** `id = biz-charity-shop`, `name = Charity Shop`, and house-style `description`/`art_notes` text; the card uses the generic fallback sprite until dedicated art is supplied.
- **Risk:** hardcoded business counts **and aggregate pool totals** are spread across many tests; missing one turns the suite red — the count updates are the largest part of the change.
- **Risk:** regenerating `expanded-card-manifest.json` and SVG artifacts produces large/generated diffs; regenerate via the documented scripts rather than hand-editing.
- **Scope-creep guard:** dedicated 1024×1024 artwork for the card is **out of scope**; if wanted, record it as a linked follow-up work item rather than expanding this one.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1: Are the stated numbers gross or net of the standard ongoing cost?**
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply during the originating intake session): A** — 1.5 is gross `baseIncome`; `baseIncome = 150`, `ongoingCost = 75`, net 0.75/turn. Questions recorded in comment `MS-C0MUIM7ZSS0001IW4` on this item.
- **Q2: Which synergy type should the Charity Shop belong to?**
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply during the originating intake session): C** — `Culture`. Questions recorded in comment `MS-C0MUIM7ZSS0001IW4`.
- **Q3: Which progression tier, and should it have an upgrade path?**
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply during the originating intake session): A** — `tier = 2`, standalone (`upgradePath = Charity Shop`, `maxLevel = 1`). Questions recorded in comment `MS-C0MUIM7ZSS0001IW4`.
- **Note:** these answers were carried over from the originating (core-repo) intake; the producer should confirm them alongside the corrected paths/counts at the next review.
- **Non-blocking assumptions:** `id`/`name`/`description`/`art_notes` and fallback-art usage were proposed in the questions comment and **not corrected** by the producer; they are treated as accepted defaults unless the producer objects.

## Summary

Add a hover tooltip to the persistent synergy lines drawn between adjacent
synergistic businesses on the Main Street board. Hovering a line explains the
shared synergy type and the per-turn effect that link has on each of the two
connected cards.

## User Story

As a Main Street player, I want to hover over a synergy line and see what that
synergy does — the shared type and the coins/reputation each linked business
gains from it — so that I can understand *why* two businesses are connected and
plan my street deliberately, instead of guessing from the line colour alone.

## Problem Statement

The board draws coloured synergy lines between adjacent businesses that share a
synergy type, but the lines are purely decorative: hovering them does nothing.
The player sees that two cards are linked but not which synergy type they share,
the rate that applies, or the value of that specific connection. The only
synergy information available today is the per-card `Synergy: <types>` line in
the business-slot tooltip, which does not explain the link or its magnitude.

## Existing State

- `drawSynergyLines()` in
  `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` draws a
  two-pass `Phaser.GameObjects.Graphics` line (core + glow) per synergy pair and
  adds it to `streetContainer`. The graphics objects are **not interactive** —
  there is no input handler on them.
- `computeSynergyPairs()` in `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacencyNeighbors.ts`
  returns `SynergyPair { fromIndex, toIndex, sharedSynergy }`, the data the
  renderer iterates to draw each line. Sold cards still participate as pair
  endpoints (CG-0MT5XUE2200047IJ).
- Per-card synergy maths lives in
  `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts`:
  `computeSynergyBonus()` (coin), `computeSynergyRepBonus()` (reputation),
  `effectiveSynergyCoinBonus()` / `effectiveSynergyRepBonus()`. The difficulty
  multiplier is `config.synergyBonusPerNeighbor`.
- Existing formatting helpers live in
  `example-games/main-street/MainStreetFormatting.ts` (`effectiveSynergyRate()`,
  `formatSynergyRate()`, `formatPerTurnReputation()`, `formatCurrency()`).
- Business-slot tooltips already use the shared `TooltipManager`
  (`s.tooltipManager?.show(info, x, y)` / `.hide()`); the manager is created
  only when `!s.replayMode`
  (`MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts`) and already honours the
  `settingsPanel.showTooltips` toggle.

## Desired Change

1. Add a pure, unit-testable content builder — e.g.
   `buildSynergyLinkTooltipInfo(grid, fromIndex, toIndex, sharedSynergy, config, soldSlots?, gridDims?)`
   in `MainStreetFormatting.ts` — that returns the tooltip text for one link.
2. In `drawSynergyLines()`, give each line a **narrow, invisible interactive hit
   area** (parented into `streetContainer`, drawn/recreated with the rest of the
   street layer) wired to `tooltipManager.show(...)` on `pointerover` and
   `tooltipManager.hide()` on `pointerout`.
3. Guard the wiring the same way existing slot tooltips are: no tooltip in
   `replayMode` and no tooltip when `tooltipManager` is absent; the
   `showTooltips` setting continues to be enforced by `TooltipManager` itself.
4. Ensure the hit area does not swallow the existing business-slot hover/click
   interactions except immediately along the line (see Constraints).

### Suggested tooltip format (implementation may refine wording)

```
Food synergy
Bakery  ⟷  Diner
Bakery: +2 coins/turn from this link
Diner: +1 coins/turn from this link
+5 reputation/turn  (only when a reputation-synergy contribution exists)
```

Sold endpoints are called out explicitly, e.g.
`Bakery (sold): earns nothing, but still anchors this synergy`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Hovering a persistent synergy line shows a tooltip that names the shared
  synergy type and states the per-turn coin and/or reputation effect of that
  link for **each** endpoint, computed with the active difficulty multiplier
  (`config.synergyBonusPerNeighbor`).
- The tooltip is hidden when the pointer leaves the line, and is not shown at
  all in replay mode; the existing `settingsPanel.showTooltips = false` toggle
  suppresses it (via `TooltipManager`).
- A sold endpoint is represented correctly: it earns nothing from the link
  itself, while the link still anchors synergy for the other endpoint, and the
  tooltip says so.
- The line hover hit area does not break the existing business-slot
  interactions: slot hover tooltips, click-to-place, sell, and upgrade
  targeting continue to work everywhere except the line's immediate vicinity.
- Unit tests cover the pure `buildSynergyLinkTooltipInfo()` builder (shared
  type, coin-only, reputation, sold endpoint, zero-synergy opt-out, difficulty
  multiplier) and an automated test covers the hover wiring on a rendered line.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Reuse the shared `TooltipManager` (`@ui`) — do **not** add a bespoke tooltip
  renderer, consistent with
  [Standardize TooltipManager across all games] (CG-0MPKE6W1C0047A44) and
  [Tooltip single-source fix] (CG-0MTJP6RNL008LGF3).
- Keep the content builder **pure** (no Phaser/scene dependency) so it can be
  unit-tested headless, mirroring `synergyLineEndpoints.ts`.
- Synergy lines are drawn **after** the slot rectangles in `drawSynergyLines()`,
  so their hit areas sit on top of the slot hit zones. The hit area must be
  narrow (a thin band around the segment, thick enough for a mouse but not so
  thick that it steals slot hover) and the chosen thickness/approach must be
  documented in a code comment.
- Hit areas are recreated on every `streetContainer` rebuild (the street layer
  is rebuilt by `refreshAll()`), so their creation must not leak listeners or
  leave stale objects behind.
- Reduced-motion: no animation is introduced; the tooltip appears/hides
  immediately, so reduced-motion preferences are unaffected.
- No new engine-level (`src/`) API is expected — Main Street-local formatting +
  renderer wiring only.
- Out of scope: tooltips on the transient synergy-formation animation line,
  changing the synergy formula, and changing line geometry/colours.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — Add an
  interactive hit area per synergy pair inside `drawSynergyLines()` and wire it
  to `s.tooltipManager`.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — New pure
  `buildSynergyLinkTooltipInfo()` builder (shared synergy type + per-endpoint
  coin/reputation effect).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacencyScoring.ts` — Reuse/extract the
  per-link contribution maths if a per-neighbour share helper is needed
  (avoid duplicating the synergy formula).
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetAdjacencyNeighbors.ts` — Source of
  `SynergyPair`; may need no change beyond typing.
- `tests/main-street/synergy-tooltip.test.ts` — New unit tests for the content
  builder.
- `tests/main-street/synergy-tooltip.browser.test.ts` — New browser test for
  hover wiring (or extend `tests/main-street/synergy-visuals.test.ts`).
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — Document the synergy-line tooltip
  interaction.
- `example-games/main-street/README.md` — Mention the tooltip in the synergy
  overview (if the README describes synergy lines).

## Risks and Assumptions

- **Assumption (documented, producer may adjust):** "the effect of that synergy"
  means the shared type plus the per-link per-turn coin/reputation contribution
  for each endpoint, rather than a generic rules paragraph. The suggested
  format above is a proposal; wording can change without altering the ACs.
- **Risk — per-link vs. card-total mismatch:** `computeSynergyBonus()` rounds
  the *total* across all matching neighbours, so a per-link share may not sum
  exactly to the displayed card total. The tooltip must not imply a precision
  it does not have; document the chosen presentation (per-link share formatted
  to at most one decimal, or card total) in the builder's doc comment.
- **Risk — input interception:** adding interactive objects on top of the slot
  hit zones can regress slot hover/click. Mitigation: narrow hit band + an
  explicit regression test for slot hover/click; keep the band culled with the
  line.
- **Risk — re-render churn:** `drawSynergyLines()` runs on every refresh; a
  fresh hit area per refresh must be destroyed with the container or it leaks.
- **Scope-creep guard:** any desire to also tooltip the *animated* formation
  line, restyle lines, or change synergy values must be filed as a separate
  work item, not folded into this one.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MM4REC2Z0GS2YKT** – Main Street: PRD Milestone 2 -- Full Content and Crafting/Building System (completed)
- **CG-0MQQHCJJ5009AB4X** – Fix Lighting Spike scene visibility (completed)
- **CG-0MQOBJ9BW006TTJR** – Main Street score tooltip should show calculation breakdown (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `CHANGELOG.md` — matched: effect, lines, provide, should, showing (+2 more)
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — matched: effect, lines, provide, should, showing (+2 more)
- `example-games/gym/README.md` — matched: effect, lines, provide, should, showing (+2 more)

### Manual related references

- **CG-0MQQHBZ3D002J02E** – Add visual synergy lines between adjacent businesses
  (completed): introduced the lines this work item makes interactive.
- **CG-0MSVM3WCD007BRQP** – Synergy lines drawn edge-to-edge / corner-to-corner
  (completed): `synergyLineEndpoints.ts` geometry reused for the hit band.
- **CG-0MT5XUE2200047IJ** – Main Street sold businesses still provide synergy
  (completed): defines sold-endpoint semantics the tooltip must reflect.
- **CG-0MPKE6W1C0047A44** – Standardize TooltipManager across all games
  (completed): the shared tooltip component to reuse.
- **CG-0MTJP6RNL008LGF3** – Tooltip single-source fix (completed): tooltip
  content should come from shared formatters.
- **CG-0MT5Y9AD2001MKWZ** – Tooltips on businesses are confusing (completed):
  precedent for clarifying Main Street tooltip wording.
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — synergy line visual/audio spec
  (lines, coin flights, animation) to extend with the tooltip.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive interview round was required: the seed context and the existing
Main Street code path (`drawSynergyLines` → `SynergyPair` → per-card synergy
formula → `TooltipManager`) were sufficient to draft a clear brief. The single
open design decision was resolved by documented assumption:

- **Assumption A1 (tooltip content):** the tooltip shows the shared synergy
  type and the per-link per-turn coin/reputation contribution for each
  endpoint, rather than a generic rules sentence. Rationale: this matches the
  wording "showing the effect of that synergy" and the precedent set by
  [Add scoring tooltip to expedition column headers] (CG-0MLXCSSES11VPL3C),
  which surfaces the live contribution rather than a definition. Source:
  repo evidence (`SynergyPair.sharedSynergy`, `computeSynergyBonus`,
  `computeSynergyRepBonus`). **OPEN QUESTION for the producer:** confirm the
  proposed format, or specify an alternative (e.g. show the card's *total*
  synergy bonus instead of the per-link share).

# Intake Brief: Serial Seller challenge (MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J)

**Headline:** Add a run-local **Serial Seller** challenge that completes when the player sells 3 or more street businesses in a single game, with live progress in the challenge HUD and a persistent Steam achievement consistent with the existing 12 challenges.

## Problem statement

Main Street's challenge pool currently has no goal that rewards _selling_ businesses, so the sell mechanic (Manage Card → Sell) is rarely a deliberate strategic path. This item adds a new run-local challenge, **Serial Seller**, that completes when the player sells 3 or more businesses in a single game, and shows live progress toward the goal in the challenge HUD.

## Users

- **Main Street players** choosing a strategy each run.
- **Main Street players** who need to gauge progress at a glance.
- **The designer/producer**, who wants the new challenge consistent with the existing challenge/achievement system.

Example user stories:

- As a Main Street player, I want a challenge that rewards selling businesses, so that a sell-and-reinvest strategy is a viable route to bonus points.
- As a player, I want to see my progress toward the challenge (e.g. "2/3 sold"), so I know how close I am to completing it.
- As the producer, I want the new challenge mapped to a persistent Steam achievement like the other 12 challenges, so the achievement set stays complete and consistent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- New challenge template and category: `ch-serial-seller` (title **Serial Seller**, description "Sell 3 or more businesses in a single game.") is added to `CHALLENGE_TEMPLATES` with `category: 'economic'` and `rewardPoints === CHALLENGE_BONUS_POINTS`; a new `economic` member is added to the `ChallengeCategory` union; its evaluator returns `true` iff the cumulative count of sold street businesses in the run is `>= 3`, and `false` on an empty grid.
- System integration and progress UI: the template participates in deterministic `selectChallenges` selection; completing it fires exactly once through `evaluateChallengesAfterAction` (bonus points awarded, activity-log entry written, persistent-achievement bridge invoked); the challenge HUD tracker renders live progress (e.g. `2/3`) for progress-capable challenges while challenges without progress metadata render unchanged.
- Undo/redo consistency: undoing a street sale reverts both the progress count and any challenge completion it caused; redo re-applies them exactly once (no double completion, no stale progress).
- Achievement mapping and cross-repo dependency: `ch-serial-seller` maps to achievement id `serial-seller` in `CHALLENGE_TO_ACHIEVEMENT_ID`; the blocking dependency work item (`MS-0MUOLL8W2004A3D7`, discovered-from this item) supplies the `core` submodule `electron/achievement-manifest.json` entry and the Steamworks backend API name (`TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER`); the achievement completeness/drift tests pass once the dependency has landed.
- Testing and validation: unit tests cover the evaluator (empty grid, 1/2/3 sales), selection inclusion, progress metadata, HUD progress rendering, and undo/redo.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Only street/tableau sales via the **Manage Card → Sell** dialog count (the `sellBusiness` path, tracked by `state.soldSlots`). Hand sales (`sellFromHand`) and the legacy `sellFromTableau` path are out of scope.
- **No new game-state field.** Reuse `state.soldSlots` (it is cumulative for the interactive path, because sold cards stay on the grid and cannot be closed) so save/load and command snapshots keep working unchanged.
- Existing tests assert **12** templates and category coverage for the 5 existing categories; these must be updated to 13 and (optionally) to assert `economic`. The category-coverage assertion for the original 5 categories must still hold.
- The achievement mapping is enforced by `tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts` against the launcher manifest, which lives in the **`core` git submodule (a separate repository)** — the manifest entry and Steamworks API name are handled by a separate **blocking dependency** work item `MS-0MUOLL8W2004A3D7` (producer/external action), not run-local.
- The per-run selection count (`config.challengesPerRun`, default 3) and the end-of-game scoring formula are unchanged — only the template pool grows.
- The progress indicator must fit the existing challenge panel geometry (compact single-line rows); avoid layout regressions.
- All written output in UK English.

## Existing state

- `src/MainStreetChallenges.ts` defines the `ChallengeCategory` union (`synergy`, `placement`, `resource`, `upgrade`, `cross-cutting`), 12 `CHALLENGE_TEMPLATES`, `DEFAULT_CHALLENGES_PER_RUN = 3`, and `selectChallenges`/`evaluateChallenges` wrappers over the generic `@core-engine` challenge API. Evaluators are pure functions of `MainStreetState`. Selection is seeded from `config.challengesPerRun` in `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts`.
- Challenge evaluation runs after every action (`evaluateChallengesAfterAction`) and at end of turn; completions are non-revocable during a run but are captured/restored by command snapshots (`captureSnapshot`/`restoreSnapshot` in `src/MainStreetCommands.ts`, which include `soldSlots`, `challengesCompleted`, and per-challenge completion flags).
- `state.soldSlots: boolean[]` marks sold street cards; sold cards remain on the grid as inert synergy anchors and cannot be closed, so the true-count is monotonic for the interactive path and is captured in undo snapshots.

# Reduce time upcoming event is shown

## Problem statement

During the end-of-turn routine an incident card from the Upcoming queue is revealed at board centre and held face-up for 4 seconds (`4000ms`). That hold is longer than needed: once the coin/reputation delta bubbles have finished animating, the extra wait only delays the turn. The hold should be shortened to **1 second longer than the delta-bubble animation** (target ≈ 1920ms).

## Users

- **Main Street player**: Needs the incident card shown long enough to read it and see the coin/reputation delta bubbles land, but not so long that the end-of-turn routine drags. Example user story: *As a player, I want the Upcoming incident reveal to finish shortly after its coin/reputation bubbles land, so the next turn starts promptly without me losing the ability to read the incident.*

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Shortened hold (full motion)**: `animateIncidentReveal` holds the face-up incident card for `INCIDENT_REVEAL_HOLD_MS` = **1920ms** — i.e. 1 second longer than the 920ms delta-bubble animation (600ms flight + 4 × 80ms max stagger) — replacing the previous 4000ms.
2. **Reduced motion parity**: the reduced-motion path uses the same `INCIDENT_REVEAL_HOLD_MS` value; no duplicate hardcoded duration remains.
3. **No hang / exactly-once completion**: the `onComplete` callback still fires exactly once after the shortened hold + return animation, and the turn-advance chain is never left pending.
4. **Bubbles complete before the hold ends**: the delta-bubble animation window (max 5 bubbles × 80ms stagger + 600ms flight = 920ms) finishes before the hold elapses, so bubbles are never cut off.
5. **Single named constant**: the duration is defined once in `MainStreetAnimatorTiming.ts` as a named constant, with the bubble flight/stagger values it derives from; no literal `4000` remains for the reveal hold.
6. **Testing/validation**: unit tests assert the new hold duration and the constant relationship (`hold = flights + stagger × (maxBubbles − 1) + 1000`); the incident-reveal browser test's timing expectations are updated to the shortened choreography.
7. **Documentation updated**: all related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. **Full suite green**: the full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Turn-advance chain preserved**: the shortened hold must still fire `onComplete` exactly once; the turn must never hang or double-advance.
- **Bubble readability**: the new hold must not truncate the delta-bubble animation (target 1920ms > 920ms bubble window).
- **Reduced-motion preserved**: reduced-motion players must still get a readable hold (no flight/flip/bubbles, but the hold remains) — per the original design (CG-0MTW18KFK000MM3I).
- **Replay/headless unchanged**: replay mode remains a no-op that still fires `onComplete`.
- **No incident**: when no incident resolves, the animation stays a complete no-op (no delay added).

## Existing state

- `MainStreetAnimatorIncident.ts` → `animateIncidentReveal()` contains the hold as a hardcoded `4000` in two places:
  - the reduced-motion path (`s.time.delayedCall(4000, () => { cleanup(); })`), and
  - the full-motion path (after the hinge flip: `s.time.delayedCall(4000, () => { … return animation … })`).
- `animateIncidentDeltaBubbles()` launches up to 5 bubbles per resource at `i * 80ms` with a `600ms` flight — a 920ms window — using local `flightMs = 600` and literal `80` staggers.
- Nominal full choreography today: flight 550ms + hinge 260ms + hold 4000ms + return 400ms ≈ 5210ms.
- The reveal blocks the day start until the hold completes (`MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.finishTurnPresentation`).

## Desired change

1. Introduce a named hold constant (e.g. `INCIDENT_REVEAL_HOLD_MS`) in `MainStreetAnimatorTiming.ts`, derived from the bubble animation: 600ms flight + 4 × 80ms stagger + 1000ms buffer = **1920ms**. Extract the bubble flight/stagger literals into named constants so the relationship is explicit and the hold cannot silently drift shorter than the bubble window.
2. Replace both hardcoded `4000` hold delays in `animateIncidentReveal()` with the new constant (full-motion and reduced-motion paths share it).
3. Update the incident-reveal unit and browser tests to the shortened choreography (including the "4000ms hold" assertions and timing-margin comments).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncident.ts` — replace the two hardcoded `4000` hold delays in `animateIncidentReveal()`; extract the `600`/`80` bubble literals in `animateIncidentDeltaBubbles()` into named constants.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorTiming.ts` — add `INCIDENT_REVEAL_HOLD_MS` (≈1920ms) plus `INCIDENT_BUBBLE_FLIGHT_MS` (600) and `INCIDENT_BUBBLE_STAGGER_MS` (80), with a derivation comment.
- `tests/main-street/incident-reveal-animator.test.ts` — update the `delay >= 4000` hold assertions to the new constant; add an assertion tying the hold to the bubble window.
- `tests/main-street/incident-reveal.browser.test.ts` — update the choreography timing notes/margins to the shortened hold.

## Related work

- **CG-0MTW18KFK000MM3I** (completed, Tableau-Card-Engine) — *Upcoming card reveal in end-of-turn routine*: introduced the 4-second hold and bubble choreography this item shortens; its "timing is fixed: 4 seconds" constraint is deliberately superseded here.
- **CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q** (completed, Tableau-Card-Engine) — *Don't add coins/reputation/score until the end of the end-of-turn cycle*: owns the deferred-mutation / deferred HUD window that the reveal's `pendingDeltas` participates in.
- **CG-0MUA1UH3A008M4BS** (in_review, Tableau-Card-Engine) — *Reputation and coins from Upcoming should flow in the correct direction*: owns Upcoming delta routing (attached vs HUD) and the coin/reputation flights referenced by this item.
- **CG-0MT23O6W8003AXWJ** (completed, Tableau-Card-Engine) — *Income Phase: phased card-effect animations*: the phased income choreography that runs before the reveal.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Assumption** — "the animation for the coins and reputation" means the delta-bubble animation during the reveal hold (600ms flight + up to 4 × 80ms stagger = 920ms), confirmed by the operator. Target hold = 920ms + 1000ms = **1920ms**.
- **Assumption** — the reduced-motion path keeps the same 1920ms hold (rather than being shortened to ~1000ms with no bubbles), preserving readable time per the original design. Revisit with the producer only if a shorter reduced-motion hold is wanted.
- **Risk** — if the bubble count or stagger changes later, a hardcoded 1920ms could truncate the animation; mitigated by deriving the constant from the bubble flight/stagger constants.
- **Risk** — timing-based tests are brittle; the unit test should assert against the constant (not a magic number) where practical, and browser tests keep generous margins.
- **Risk** — shortening the hold interacts with the deferred HUD window and the incident-reveal → day-start chain; the exactly-once `onComplete` guarantee must be preserved.
- **Scope-creep risk** — requests to change the flight/hinge/return durations or add new reveal effects are out of scope and must be raised as separate work items.

## Clarifying questions & answers (Appendix)

- **Q1**: The description says "Reduce this to 1 second longer than the animation for the coins and reputation". Which animation is the reference point?
  - Options presented: (1) the delta-bubble animation during the incident hold (~920ms = 600ms flight + 4 × 80ms max stagger) → target ≈ 1920ms; (2) the coin flight duration (`INCOME_FLIGHT_MS` = 600ms) → target ≈ 1600ms.
  - **Answer (operator, interactive): Option 1** — the delta-bubble animation time, target hold ≈ 1920ms.
  - Evidence: `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncident.ts` (`animateIncidentDeltaBubbles`, `flightMs = 600`, stagger `i * 80`).
- **Q2** (resolved by repo inspection, no operator input needed): Where is the hold implemented and how long is it? — `animateIncidentReveal()` hardcodes `4000` in both the full-motion and reduced-motion paths. Source: code inspection.

1. `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json` contains a `serial-seller` entry with `steamApiName: TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER` and `hidden: false`.
2. The Steamworks partner backend declares the matching `TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER` achievement API name.

6. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

- The manifest lives in the `core` git submodule (a separate repository: `TheWizardsCode/Tableau-Card-Engine`), requiring two repo operations.
- The `steamApiName` values must match exactly what is configured on the Steamworks partner backend, or Steam will silently drop the unlock.
- The achievement must not be hidden (`hidden: false`), consistent with the existing 12 challenges.
- The Steamworks backend configuration is a producer/external action that must be completed independently of code changes.
